AI Summary

Three items this fortnight land squarely on lab systems. Jiang et al. resolve segregating transposable-element alleles across 231 haplotype-resolved human pangenomes with matched long-read multi-omics, moving polymorphic TEs from present/absent genotypes into actual sequences carrying methylation states and transcript contributions; their conclusion is that regulatory innovation before fixation is a mixture of gain, remodeling and loss rather than one-way accumulation. Prokopov et al. show CDK9 inhibition reactivates TEs across cancer types, and their TEgment pipeline finds the reactivated elements appear predominantly as readthrough, 3'UTR-embedded and lncRNA-embedded transcripts rather than autonomous units — the non-canonical transcript architecture thesis, stated as a genome-wide default. And Xu et al. report an insect virus that attenuates antiviral immunity by suppressing splicing to shift the STING transcription start site: alternative TSS usage in an innate immune signaling gene, deployed as a viral evasion strategy.

On TE infrastructure and loci, ERVmancer attacks the practical obstacle behind most HERV work — short reads that cannot be assigned to individual loci — with phylogeny-guided quantification that benchmarks favorably against matched long-read data and recovers p53-mediated suppression of HERVH-LTR7, directly applicable to asking which individual LTR10 copies are active in colorectal tumors. Waseem et al. reconstruct human-specific expansion and remodeling of the K111 ERV at acrocentric nucleolar organizer regions, with parent-offspring trios capturing remodeling and de novo sequence exchange between generations. Amano et al. build a self-splicing-intron EGFP reporter that makes Alu retrotransposition visible by flow cytometry and, in dual color, alongside L1. At the macroevolutionary end, Schrader et al. use 163 ant genomes to tie convergent TE acquisition bursts to the radiations following the K-Pg extinction, and Bouanich et al. find a quantitative relationship between nearby Copia/Gypsy insertions and ohnolog under-expression in apple.

An unusually dense STING block runs through the journal slate, all of it trafficking and turnover rather than sensing: Hou et al. identify ACTA2 actin filaments as the transport system licensing STING's ER-to-Golgi move, Dominguez-Martin et al. place mitochondrial Fis1 upstream of Rab7A in STING's endolysosomal degradation, and Li et al. show a coronavirus nucleocapsid blocking DAD1-dependent STING phosphorylation. Gao et al. add a chromatin-side brake, with nuclear cGAS repressing inflammatory transcription through HDAC1 independently of STING. Two enhancer papers bear on regulatory variation at immune loci: Majumder et al. dissect the HLA-DR/DQ super enhancer into five competing microelements in the most polymorphic region of the genome, and Zhao et al. catalogue 557,310 cCREs across Crohn's ileum and colon, localizing heritability to T cells and neutrophils in the same inflamed GI tissue context as the LTR10 work. TRIM28 surfaces twice in non-TE guise — as a Pol II cofactor in Jang et al. and as a druggable E3 scaffold in Su et al..

On the isoform and methods side, Cohen et al. extend MERFISH to roughly 10,000 isoforms imaged in intact tissue, and Testa et al. supply a Bayesian method for quantifying isoform abundance at the protein level — the half of the IFNAR2 decoy receptor argument that transcript data alone cannot make. Merrill et al. and Mehta et al. both show transcript architecture setting phenotype, through PRMT1-SFPQ-dependent intron retention feeding NMD and through synaptotagmin 7 splice variants that differ in phase separation behavior. Partel et al. transfer Enformer and Borzoi representations onto single-cell multiome atlases so sequence-to-function models can simulate perturbations, SVPG accelerates pangenome graph augmentation and structural variant calling, and McKinlay et al. co-measure contacts, methylation and accessibility on single nanopore molecules. One caution worth flagging: Modolo et al. show CUT&Tag systematically loses H3K36me3 and H3K27me3 signal in GC-poor regions while over-reporting in hyperaccessible chromatin — a bias that lands directly on repeat families with skewed GC content.
